lesson.menu_desc: Pedir ajuda a um estranho sem pedir desculpas demais: Excuse me e Do you know where ... is? -- 30 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 21 -- Asking for Help in Public
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Patrícia Yamaguti | Lesson 21 -- Asking for Help in Public
lesson.grammar_point: indirect questions with do you know where and do you know if for asking strangers

listenings.text: I live in the city, and tourists ask me for help every day, and I like it. Really, it is no problem. But here is my tip. Start with excuse me. Then say sorry to bother you, one time, only one. Some people say sorry five times, and then I do not know what they need. After that, ask your question in a short way. The best question is: do you know where something is? Do you know where the station is? Do you know where the restroom is? It is polite, and it is easy for me, because I can say yes and show you, or say no and you can ask somebody else. And at the end, a smile and thank you. That is all. Thirty seconds, and everybody is happy.

Good afternoon, and welcome to Harbor Mall. Here is some information for our visitors today. The restrooms on Level 2 are closed for cleaning until four o'clock. Please use the restrooms on Level 3, next to the cinema. If your phone battery is low, there is a free charging station in the café on Level 1, and you can buy chargers at TechCorner on the same floor. If you lose a child, please do not run. Go to the Help Point near the main doors, or talk to any person in a blue shirt. We are here to help. Thank you, and have a nice day.

extra_audio.text: Excuse me, sorry to bother you. Do you know where the restroom is? And do you know if there is a pharmacy nearby? Could you take a photo of us, please? Thank you so much. You are very kind.
